questions.prompt:
A quantity is modelled by $V=1200(1.08)^t$, where $t$ is measured in years.
(a) State the percentage change per year. (1)
(b) Find $V$ when $t=3$. (2)
(c) Find, to the nearest whole year, the first value of $t$ for which $V>2000$. (3)
(d) Explain one limitation of using this model for a long period of time. (2)
hints: Read the multiplier as 1 + growth rate.
Use logarithms to solve an exponential inequality.
questions.solution:
(a) The annual increase is $8\%$.
(b) $V=1200(1.08)^3\approx1511.65$.
(c) Solve $1200(1.08)^t>2000$: $t>6.637$, so the first whole year is 7.
(d) A constant percentage growth assumption is unlikely to remain valid indefinitely because real conditions change.

questions.prompt:
The polynomial $p(x)=x^3-5x^2+8x-4$ has a factor $(x-2)$.
(a) Verify this using the factor theorem. (2)
(b) Hence factorise $p(x)$ fully. (3)
(c) Solve $p(x)=0$. (2)
hints: Use p(a)=0 for the factor theorem.
Then divide the cubic by the known linear factor.
questions.solution:
Substitution gives $p(2)=0$, so $(x-2)$ is a factor. Dividing gives $(x-1)(x-2)$, hence $p(x)=(x-2)(x-1)(x-2)$. Therefore the roots are $x=2,1,2$.

questions.prompt:

(a) Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$. (2)

(c) Find the equation of the tangent at the point where $x=1$. (3)
hints: Differentiate each power term.

questions.solution:

The line $L$ has equation $y=2x+5$.
(a) Find the equation of the line through $(2,9)$ perpendicular to $L$. (3)

(c) Find the exact distance from $(0,5)$ to $(2,9)$. (2)
hints: Perpendicular gradients multiply to -1.

questions.solution:
A perpendicular gradient is $-1/2$. Using point-gradient form gives $y-(9)=-\frac1{2}(x-2)$.

Distance $=\sqrt{2^2+(4)^2}=\sqrt{20}$.

questions.prompt:
$\mathbf{a}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\9\end{pmatrix}$.
(a) Show that $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are parallel. (2)
Points $P,Q,R$ have position vectors $\mathbf{p}$, $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{b}$.
(b) Find the ratio $PQ:PR$. (2)
(c) Explain what this tells you about the positions of $P,Q,R$. (3)
hints: Look for a scalar multiple.
Positive scalar multiples point in the same direction.
questions.solution:
$\mathbf{b}=3\mathbf{a}$, so the vectors are parallel. Hence $PR=3PQ$, so $PQ:PR=1:3$. Since the displacement vectors are positive scalar multiples, $P,Q,R$ are collinear and $Q$ lies between $P$ and $R$.

questions.prompt:
A bag contains 4 red counters and 6 blue counters. Two counters are taken without replacement.
(a) Find the probability that both are red. (2)
(b) Find the probability that the two counters are different colours. (3)
(c) Given that at least one counter is red, find the probability that both are red. (2)
hints: The second denominator is one less because there is no replacement.
Use conditional probability for part (c).
questions.solution:
(a) $P(RR)=\frac{4}{10}\times\frac{3}{9}=0.1333$.
(b) Add $P(RB)$ and $P(BR)$, giving $0.5333$.
(c) $P(RR\mid\text{at least one R})=P(RR)/P(\text{at least one R})=0.2000$.
